MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY
PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid (uncultured)
Gestational Age: 32 weeks
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal aneuploidy screening

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniotic fluid cells using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. Multiple informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S858, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1437
- Sex chromosomes: AMELX/Y, SRY, XHPRT, X22

PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated for heterozygous markers.

RESULTS
Chromosome 13: Two alleles detected for all informative markers - NORMAL
Chromosome 18: Two alleles detected for all informative markers - NORMAL
Chromosome 21: Two alleles detected for all informative markers - NORMAL
Sex Chromosomes: XY pattern detected - MALE FETUS

Molecular Karyotype: rsa(X,Y)×1,(13,18,21)×2

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates a normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 with a male sex chromosome pattern (XY). No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) was detected.

LIMITATIONS
- This test only screens for whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected
- Segmental imbalances, balanced rearrangements, and aneuploidies of other chromosomes are not detected
- Maternal cell contamination can affect results
- This test does not screen for single gene disorders

ADDITIONAL TESTING
Separate analysis for HSD3B2 gene mutations is in progress and will be reported separately.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on these results, no further chromosome analysis is indicated for the tested aneuploidies. Standard obstetric care and monitoring should continue.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
